input: nums is an array of n safe integers; empty input is accepted. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Fresh array where entry i is the number of distinct values in nums[0..i] minus the number in nums[i+1..n-1].
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state. Output is newly allocated.
numeric: Moving the current value from suffix counts to prefix membership before measuring matches the inclusive-prefix/exclusive-suffix boundary. Counts/results have magnitude at most n. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n+1) time and O(n+1) auxiliary/output space under bounded-key map/set assumptions. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 481 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline. Helpers are fully charged per candidate, not free shared libraries. No imports, runtime-generated implementations or hidden source expansion are used. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source.
